cohort: 215 pregnant women diagnosed with cervical insufficiency, who underwent emergency cervical cerclage between 19 and 27 weeks of pregnancy.
finding: Double-level cervical cerclage was found to be more effective than single-level cerclage for treating cervical insufficiency, significantly reducing premature births between 32 and 37 weeks, increasing full-term live births, and resulting in a higher newborn survival rate beyond 28 days with lower neonatal mortality.
mod_finding: Vaginal deliveries were predominant in both groups (single CC: 85.3%, double CC: 89.4%), and while the difference was not statistically significant (p>0.05), the double-level cerclage group was associated with a higher proportion of vaginal births.
birth_weight: 3087 g (single CC group), 3117 g (double CC group)
